LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Imagn Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Green Bay fell to 4-3 with a loss to Detroit in Week 7, and it's in last place in a loaded NFC North through seven weeks. Meanwhile, the Panthers (3-3) are in first place in the NFC South despite a major blowout loss at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Carolina made the playoffs in the 2025 season, but it has a ton of injuries on both sides of the ball that make it a tough team to trust against other quality opponents -- like Green Bay. Oddsmakers agree with that sentiment, as they've set the Packers as favorites at home to open this week. Panthers vs. Packers Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Panthers +3.5 (-110) Packers -3.5 (-110) Panthers: +154 Packers: -185 48.5 (Over -105/Under -115) There hasn't been a ton of movement in the odds for this game , as the Packers remain 3.5-point favorites at home. The total has jumped up from 47.5 to 48.5 while the moneyline has actually moved in Carolina's favor. According to DraftKings, just 22 percent of the moneyline bets and 41 percent of the spread bets are on the Panthers after their Week 7 showing against Tampa Bay. Earlier this week, I shared in SI Betting's preview for this game why I believe Green Bay is a worthwhile bet: The Panthers’ run defense was torched in Week 7 by Tampa Bay, and this could be a “get-right” spot for Matt LaFleur’s offense. Love should be able to attack through the air, as the Panthers are a below-average defense overall (20th in EPA/Play), and they entered Week 7 allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Meanwhile, Green Bay’s defense held a vaunted Detroit offense to just 20 points and is now fifth in the league in EPA/Play. If it weren’t for multiple missed field goals, the Pack could be entering this game with a 5-2 record. Carolina beat Detroit this season, but it has some confounding losses against Cleveland and at home against Tampa Bay. I don’t love this team – which is extremely banged up after Taylor Moton went down in Week 7 – on a short week against a Packers squad that has an above-average defense. I’m going to lay the points with a Green Bay team that needs this game a lot more than Carolina does if it’s going to make the playoffs. I'm not the only member of the SI Betting team taking Green Bay, as Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every NFL game, every week -- why he likes the Pack at home as well: I wrote about how I was out on the Panthers last week, and I proved to be right as they ended up on the wrong side of a blowout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. They cannot linger on that very long, though, because they play the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night. The vibes were so high and the Panthers were favored at home before dropping the egg of all eggs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Now, a loss puts them below .500, souring what had been a really fun start to the season. Will they lose? Here's what the early odds say for this primetime bout. NFL Week 8 odds for Panthers-Packers revealed Carolina Panthers running back Anthony Tyus III (34) runs against Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Zyon McCollum | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect To absolutely no one's surprise, the Panthers are road underdogs against the Packers. The Packers are -115 to cover, and the Panthers are -105 to cover. The over/under is set at 47.5 points, with the over at -112 and the under is -108. The Panthers are +160 to win outright, and the Packers are -192 on the moneyline. The oddsmakers don't have a lot of faith in the Panthers, despite both teams coming off a loss. Essentially, the oddsmakers believe the Packers will win with a final score of 26-22. Somewhat surprisingly, it's not expected to be a bigger blowout for the Packers. The Panthers just can't get healthy. Taylor Moton went down shortly after returning, and they're still without Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn. Meanwhile, the Packers are adding players. Josh Jacobs just returned from the Commissioner's Exempt List. He probably shook the rust off, which is bad news for a Panthers defense that now has two games allowing 250+ rushing yards to opponents under its belt. So, unfortunately, there are plenty of reasons to expect the Panthers to lose, and it's unlikely they can replicate last season's magical upset. The same formula simply won't work, and the Packers will likely not underestimate them this time. away.headline: Packers-Panthers Tuesday injury report: Time near for Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler?
away.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle). Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

away.headline: Carolina Panthers vs. Bucs: Who wins? Our predictions, injury report, TV info
away.blurb: So can the Panthers sustain their recent success? Will Mayfield’s return yield a new hope? Will the NFC South standings be shaken up? Fans can also check the game out on radio: WRFX The Fox, 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline). For full local listings, check out the Carolina Panthers Radio Network . Special note: Kuechly will receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame ring at halftime of the game in Bank of America Stadium. Out: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) Questionable: OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) Out: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield (rib) Questionable: QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) Alex Zietlow: Panthers 35, Bucs 31. I know that Baker Mayfield’s almost-certain return will make this Bucs offense more dynamic. And I know that scoring 35 on this Bucs team will be difficult, considering their opportunistic defensive backfield and their Top 5 rush defense. Still, barring an implosion of turnovers, I think the Panthers outscore and outlast a Bucs team trying to get back on track. Can the Carolina Panthers make it three wins in a row? And can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers get back on track? The Panthers (3-2) are returning to Bank of America Stadium for their Week 7 contest (1 p.m., FOX) fresh off two statement victories against the Detroit Lions and the Philadelphia Eagles . They’re looking to go 4-2 for the first time as a franchise since 2019 and start 2-0 in the NFC South for the first time since 2022. Carolina ranks first in the NFL in passing yards per game (295.6), second in total yards per game (404.4) and fourth in points per game (29.2). And its defense — minus the Week 1 fiasco against the Bears that’s looking more and more like an aberration — is Top 10 in several statistics, including rushing yards allowed. The Panthers have allowed fewer than 50 yards in each of the last two weeks: 46 against the Lions, 35 against the Eagles. It’s true that the defense is a bit affected by injury, specifically at the outside linebacker spot with no Jaelan Phillips or Thomas Incoom this week . It’s also true that the defense has only had to play against starting quarterbacks three times so far this season, and two of those three — against Caleb Williams of the Bears and Deshaun Watson of the Browns — have yielded losses. That won’t happen this week; it looks like the Bucs will be led by Baker Mayfield, who’s missed the last few weeks with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand. Speaking of the Bucs (1-5): While many of their offensive stats might be skewed by Mayfield’s absence, many of their strengths will remain. Namely? Their rush defense. Tampa Bay ranks second in the NFL in rush yards allowed per game at 75.5, thanks to a defensive line anchored by nose tackle Vita Vea and an entire unit led by rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter. home.headline: Packers-Panthers Tuesday injury report: Time near for Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler?
home.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle). Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

home.blurb: Packers WR Matthew Golden was a limited participant in Green Bay's Wednesday practice session, making him questionable for Thursday night. Unfortunately, one of the Packers' key players suffered an injury in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. Golden was checked out in the middle of the game for a foot injury. That's on top of a shoulder issue that Golden was dealing with before this game. Golden did not practice on Monday and Tuesday, raising concerns that the star might not be able to play in a short week. However, there's some good news coming for the Packers and for fantasy football owners in Week 8. Golden was a limited participant in Green Bay's Wednesday practice session. He also comes into the game with a questionable designation, per Rob Demovsky. This could mean that Golden might be able to suit up against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night. home.headline: Packers injury report: Jordan Love upgraded, 2 defensive starters added
home.blurb: Love, who is dealing with back soreness coming out of last Sunday's win over the Dallas Cowboys, got in a full padded practice on Thursday. He said Wednesday that he had no concerns over his availability for Sunday's showdown with the Detroit Lions , and Love's upgraded practice status on Thursday appears to confirm his belief. Barring a setback, he'll start against the Lions at Ford Field. Two defensive starters are dealing with new issues: Franklin has a shin injury, while Van Ness has an illness. It's currently unclear if either player is in danger of missing Sunday. More information will be available come Friday, when Matt LaFleur answers questions from the media before practice and before the Packers release a final injury report. Last week, safety Evan Williams was able to get through an illness and play well against the Cowboys. The only player who did not participate for the Packers at practice on Thursday was receiver Bo Melton, who is dealing with a back injury. He can be assumed out for Sunday unless he practices in some capacity on Friday. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle) and Matthew Golden (shoulder) both practiced in a limited capacity. LaFleur said both would play Sunday against the Lions. home.headline: Former Packers Draft Bust Gets Terminated by Current NFL Team
home.blurb: Deguara, the Packers’ 2020 third-round selection (94th overall) out of Cincinnati, spent four seasons in Green Bay before the team allowed him to depart as an unrestricted free agent following the 2023 season. An ACL injury limited him to two games as a rookie. His best year came in 2021, when he recorded 25 receptions for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Production declined steadily afterward: 13 catches for 114 yards in 2022 and just eight for 65 yards in 2023. His path since leaving Titletown has been one of fleeting opportunities and limited impact, reinforcing the front office’s decision to move on. For Packers fans, the news serves mainly as a quiet postscript on a draft pick that never panned out. The Green Bay Packers are hoping that emerging star pass rusher Rashan Gary can return the form that he showed in 2022 in 2023. Selected with the idea of contributing as a versatile H-back in Matt LaFleur’s offense—complete with blocking grit and occasional receiving flashes—he never developed into a reliable contributor. Across his Packers tenure, he totaled roughly 47 receptions for 436 yards and two scores while logging significant special-teams snaps as his offensive role diminished. The selection, which raised eyebrows even at the time given the modest draft value traditionally placed on H-backs, stands as a clear miss relative to the draft capital expended. Green Bay later found more productive answers at tight end, most notably with Tucker Kraft, leaving Deguara’s tenure as a reminder of earlier trial and error at the position. After Green Bay, Deguara bounced between the Jacksonville Jaguars, Arizona Cardinals, San Francisco 49ers, New York Giants, and Philadelphia Eagles, never establishing a consistent offensive role and functioning primarily as a special-teams depth piece. Career totals sit at 53 receptions for 471 yards and three touchdowns in approximately 78 games. picks.blurb: Ravens get good news on Lamar Jackson's odds to play vs. Bills and Josh Allen - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers win World Series NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Matt Sullivan Tue, October 27, 2026 at 8:45 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens have been without Lamar Jackson for three weeks now, and they clearly need him back. They got out to a 13-0 lead in Week 7, a week Jackson seemed very likely to suit up for. But they blew the lead, and now sit at 4-3. Will the Ravens get Jackson back for Week 8 when they face off against the Buffalo Bills ? It's hard to say with the shaky nature of this ankle injury for Jackson, but on Tuesday, the Ravens got some good news. According to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport , Jackson is expected to play in Week 8 against the Bills. For the first time since his ankle injury, Jackson is close to 100% healthy, which bodes well for his odds to suit up this upcoming week. Ravens get good news on Lamar Jackson for Week 8 "First of all, I expect based on the people I've spoken with that Lamar Jackson will play this week," Rapoport said. "He'll be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills." There is finally some good news for the Ravens on the Jackson injury front, as he's seemingly finally set to come back and suit up for Baltimore in Week 8. He's missed three games with an ankle injury, but is closing in on a return to the field for Week 8. While it's not yet confirmed by the Ravens or Jackson, this report is a huge sign things are trending in the right direction. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ' Jonathan Taylor Rapoport added to his report, revealing that "He is believed to be as close to 100% as he's been, and the Ravens do expect him to play." With Rapoport reporting that Jackson is expected to play and that he's close to being 100% for this week's upcoming matchup against the Bills, it seems likely Jackson is good to go. Facing the Bills in Week 8, the Ravens are expected to have Jackson back at quarterback over Tyler Huntley. It's not yet official, but this is the most positive sign that Jackson is coming back. The Baltimore Ravens are trending toward getting Lamar Jackson back for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Jackson has missed each of the team's last three games after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that stretch, losing each of their last two matchups against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Wednesday, Jackson started the week of practice with full participation. away.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson expected to play in Week 8: report
away.blurb: Jackson was able to notch limited practice participation leading up to this past Sunday’s Week 7 loss to the Bengals, but he was ultimately ruled out. Now, the Ravens are gearing up for a highly-anticipated Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed each of the last three games after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that span with Tyler Huntley at the helm, dropping each of their last two games against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Tuesday, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport confidently reported that Jackson will be on the field for this Week 8 clash. “I expect, based on the people that I’ve spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He will be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills,” Rapoport said. “I know we’ve been here before. This was a 2-3 week injury — he’s through the third week. He is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been and the Ravens do expect him to play.” With Jackson off the field, the Ravens have dropped to last place in the AFC North standings with a 4-3 record. They’ll look to get back in the win column in a difficult road matchup against the Bills this coming Sunday. Sunday’s game will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. The Ravens then have a short week to prepare for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. away.headline: Ravens Week 7 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Left Early With Injury
away.blurb: The first-round interior offensive lineman's return to his natural position at right guard after playing the last three games at center was short-lived and cut short due to injury. After taking a knee to his right knee while making a block downfield, he left the game following that drive and did not return. It marked the first time all season that he missed a single snap on offense, as he only played 16 of the Ravens' 67 total snaps on that side of the ball. According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Ioane suffered a sprained MCL, and while it's not a long-term injury, he is expected to miss time. Head coach Jesse Minter alluded to the fact that he'll likely miss this week's massive matchup against the Buffalo Bills following Wednesday's practice. "We'll see where it's at with (Vega)," Minter said. "If there's anybody that can do something crazy and overcome things, he's got the right mentality. We'll see how that goes, and we'll put the best guy out there that gives us the best opportunity for this particular game." The third-rounder picked up where he left off in his return from injury last week by picking up key first-down conversions on the first two of the three receptions that he made on five targets for 25 receiving yards. All three came on third down, with the first being a juggling snag he gained control of before backpedaling out of bounds for a gain of 10 yards on the Ravens' second scoring drive. Two plays later, he came up clutch again with a nine-yard snag on third-and-medium that he had to go low to pluck before it could hit the ground. His third catch came on the final play of the third quarter with the Ravens deep in Bengals territory, and had he not had to work back to the quarterback after getting sufficient depth at the top of his route, Lane likely would've been 3-for-3 on third-down conversions as he dragged down two yards shy of the line to gain. Lane nearly had a mulligan on recording his first career touchdown catch on the Ravens' last possession of the first half on a third-and-short in the low red zone. Unfortunately, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley's pass was just out of reach of the long-limbed wideout, who got nice separation from the corner guarding him on the play. away.headline: Ravens hope Lamar Jackson returns for rematch with Bills
away.blurb: With Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) nearing a return after a three-game absence, Bills quarterback Josh Allen is looking forward to another intense contest. "When I talked about it being flat on the sidelines, when we don't have energy or things are not going the way they're supposed to, somebody has to bring that spark, whether it's speaking or out there on the field making a play that turns everything around. That's what I need to do." Buffalo wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) was a limited practice participant on Wednesday after missing the past two games. Right tackle Spencer Brown (back) missed the session. Among other limited participants were defensive tackle Ed Oliver (knee), outside linebacker Bradley Chubb (chest/thumb) and tight end Dalton Kincaid (chest). For Baltimore, star linebacker Roquan Smith and standout safety Kyle Hamilton both sat out with knee injuries. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins and guard Olaivavega Ioane also missed the session with knee injuries. Stanley (toe/ankle) and defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) were among the Ravens who were limited in practice. That matchup was the rematch of the previous season's AFC divisional playoff game, best remembered for Ravens tight end Mark Andrews dropping a tying two-point conversion attempt late in the game. The Bills (5-1) will see if good fortune is still on their side when they again battle the Ravens (4-3) on Sunday at Orchard Park, N.Y. After winning the previous postseason meeting 27-25, Buffalo rallied from a 15-point fourth-quarter deficit in September 2025 before Matt Prater kicked the winning field goal as time expired. "The competitor in you wants to compete against the best of the best," Allen said of Jackson on Wednesday. "Since Lamar entered the league, he's been one of the best quarterbacks. What he's consistently done when he's on the field is unbelievable. He's a very special player and I have a lot of respect for him." Allen, the 2024 NFL MVP, passed for 394 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for two scores in the 2025 matchup. Jackson, a two-time MVP, passed for 209 yards and two touchdowns and added 70 yards and one score on the ground. Jackson practiced in full Wednesday as he worked toward returning from his ankle injury. Baltimore is 1-2 without him, including consecutive setbacks in which it didn't score a single second-half point. "It's going to be a big boost," Ravens left tackle Ronnie Stanley said of Jackson possibly being on the field. "Lamar is the best player in the NFL. We all know how good of a player he is, but we also don't want to rely on him having to carry us as a team." Baltimore averaged 29 points during Jackson's four starts and that number dipped to 17.7 during three starts with backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley. Baltimore led Cincinnati 13-0 at halftime Sunday before surrendering five consecutive touchdowns in a 35-13 home loss. Baltimore star running back Derrick Henry, who rushed for 169 yards and two touchdowns against the Bills

away.blurb: Ravens Week 7 Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Officially Limited - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Week 7 Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Officially Limited Despite quarterback Lamar Jackson not practicing during the media portion of practice, he apparently did some limited work. As stated above, Jackson practiced in a limited fashion . Head coach Jesse Minter also said the quarterback did some work with the team as well. Jackson was officially limited with his ankle. Whether or not that means he can play on Sunday remains to be seen. The good news for the Ravens is that the passer was limited, as opposed to not practicing. Wide receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder), safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), tight end Matthew Hibner (hand), guard Vega Ioane (ankle), guard John Simpson (groin), tackle Ronnie Stanley (rest, toe, ankle), cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee), guard Andrew Vorhees (foot), and defensive lineman Broderick Washington (ankle) were all limited. If Ioane's ankle leads to him being ruled out, it would lead to Vorhees potentially taking over. However, Vorhees is also dealing with a foot injury that has led to him missing the last two games. If the worst-case scenario happens for the Ravens' line, it would be Emery Jones Jr. stepping in yet again as the team's right guard. Jones has filled in with Ioane stepping in at center and Vorhees being out due to injury. (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:37 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are gearing up to face the Cincinnati Bengals, and the team has released its initial injury report. The full injury report is as follows: The only two players who did not participate on Wednesday is veteran defensive lineman Calais Campbell, who had veteran rest, and linebacker Tavius Robinson, who is dealing with a pectoral injury. Hibner has returned to practice after missing Week 6 due to a hand injury. A bigger issue is Ioane appearing on the injury report with an ankle ailment. He has served as the team's emergency center, but it does appear that Cam Jurgens is returning. Jurgens did not have a red no-contact jersey on at practice, and Minter stated the team is "excited" to get him on the field as the team's center. If Jurgens can line up as the team's center, that would lead to Ioane returning to the right guard position. This is assuming that Ioane can also suit up. Some better news is that Tampa is also working his way back from injury. The cornerback suffered a knee injury in Week 1 that has sidelined him since then. Baltimore has an important matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Losing two divisional matchups might come back to haunt the Ravens at the end of the season.

Now he is saying he rested through practice in Week 6 so he would be available when the Bills faced the Las Vegas Raiders. He is still sore, still resting – three weeks later. The Buffalo Bills got back to work on Wednesday. The hope has widely been that the bye week would give some added rest to players who had been nursing bumps, bruises, and those injuries that were keeping them from going full speed. While we see one name returning for the first time this season, an extra week of rest may not have been enough for another. _____________________________________________________________________________ OLB Bradley Chubb (chest/thumb) WR Tyrell Shavers – PUP – (knee) There’s plenty of good news in this group. Buffalo opened the 21-day practice window on Shavers. The wide receiver had ACL surgery in late January. He now has until the week before Thanksgiving to get back on the roster. Alford hasn’t healed and Chubb, who noticeably missed some snaps in Week 6, added a chest injury to his list of ailments. The bigger concern is Dalton Kincaid. This is his fourth season in the NFL and we are still looking for a full year of games from him. He did play in 16 his rookie season, but missed four and five the next two years respectively. Bills players with full practice: G Ar’maj Reed-Adams (back/elbow) S C.J. Gardner Johnson (suspended) We can’t be certain that Gardner Johnson’s injury is no longer a problem as he serves a one-week suspension stemming from an on-field altercation in Las Vegas. But an extra week of healing time should help Here’s a look at what the Ravens are dealing with this week. Lamar Jackson is back to practice, as expected. The quarterback has been dealing with a high ankle sprain for the past month causing him to miss the last three games. It looks like he plans to play in Buffalo this weekend.

Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 28, 2026, 5:04 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans will face the Cincinnati Bengals in NFL Week 8 following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns. The Bengals' passing offense, led by quarterback Joe Burrow, poses a significant challenge to the Titans' struggling defense. Positives are hard to find amid the Tennessee Titans’ struggles, but running back Tony Pollard was one last week. The Memphis native had his second-best game as a Titans player, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 25 carries in a gutting 27-24 home loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Maybe Pollard can do it again when the Titans (1-6) face the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS) in NFL Week 8. The Bengals' and Browns ' run defenses are about the same statistically. Cincinnati allows 116.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 19th in the league. The Titans gained a season-high 322 yards of offense with Pollard’s contributions, taking pressure off developing second-year quarterback Cam Ward . Tennessee coach Robert Saleh pinned the Browns loss on defense . Now that unit will face Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who’s 11th in the league with 1,653 yards passing, and second with 15 passing touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cincinnati Bengals stat to know Cincinnati has 13 pass plays of 25 yards or more this season. Tennessee has seven. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Bengals The good news: Cincinnati’s offense ranks 29th in rushing yards per game (81.2), so there’s an opportunity for the Titans to make the Bengals one-dimensional. The bad news: Cincinnati’s offense is doing fine without a rushing threat, averaging 345.2 yards. It isn’t a big Titans advantage, but they must capitalize on it and see if stopping the run allows their pass rush to play like it did against the Colts (six sacks). It will take a stark turnaround after Tennessee allowed a season-high 183 yards rushing against the Browns. That marked the franchise’s worst single-game Pro Football Focus run defense grade (36.3) since 2023. Personnel changes up front have not helped. Run-stopping defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released on Oct. 20 after breaking the NFL's gun policy . Third-year defender Timmy Horne was signed from the practice squad to replace him. Where Cincinnati Bengals have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s secondary tackled poorly and took bad angles against the Browns, making rookie receiver KC Concepcion look like a Pro Bowler (eight catches, 129 yards). Imagine what Burrow and receivers Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase might do. The Titans haven't seen an offense like this in 2026. The Bengals are seventh in the league in passing yards per game (264) and get 76% of their total yards through the air. Higgins and Chase have accounted for nine of the Bengals’ 13 explosive pass plays. Saleh’s also soul-searching in his secondary. Alontae Taylor was signed in the offseason to fortify one of Tennessee’s outside corner spots, but he was made inactive in Week 6 by coach’s decision and didn’t see the field in Week 7. Now it looks like Taylor will likely move to nickel . This would be a good week for Taylor to make a contribution, assuming Saleh plays him. Score prediction: Bengals 35, Titans 21 The Titans' scarred defense won’t be able to slow Burrow, and they can’t depend on Ward to keep pace in a shootout. It looks like their worst-case scenario matchup. Winning the turnover battle and making a few plays on special teams would help, but the Titans will be fortunate to keep it within 14 points. away.blurb: Tennessee Titans rookie and leading receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice on Oct. 28, according to the team's injury report. DL John Franklin-Myers (Groin), DNP WR Calvin Ridley (Hip), Limited WR Carnell Tate (Shoulder), DNP P Tommy Townsend (Left Knee), DNP Tate has a team-high 34 catches for 413 yards and a touchdown this season. Tennessee (1-6) plays the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS). Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Titans punter Tommy Townsend (knee) also didn't practice after sustaining a first-half injury against the Cleveland Browns and missing the rest of the game. Tennessee signed punter Thomas Morstead to the practice squad on Oct. 28. "Tommy is still hurting from the game," Saleh said before practice. "We're not sure. We're still working through the week to see if he can make it. We signed a punter just in case. We'll know more by the end of the week." More: Tennessee Titans DT Jeffery Simmons shoots down trade rumors More: Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Townsend is averaging 49.2 yards on 30 punts through seven games. Saleh knows the 40-year-old Morstead, a fifth-round draft pick of the New Orleans Saints in 2009. Morstead played for the Saints (2019-2020), New York Jets (2021, 2023-24), Atlanta Falcons (2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), and San Francisco 49ers (2025). He was on the Indianapolis Colts practice squad earlier in the 2026 season. Saleh was the Jets coach during Morstead's time there and the defensive coordinator at San Francisco when Morstead played for the 49ers. away.headline: Ja'Marr Chase absent from Bengals' practice ahead of Week 8 vs Titans
away.blurb: Chase was in concussion protocol and listed as questionable for the Miami game. After a four-yard catch from Burrow against Jacksonville, Chase had his facemask grabbed by Jags defensive back Jarrian Jones . Chase went to the ground and took a big hit from linebacker Ventrell Miller. Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase didn't join the rest of the team for its stretch at practice Oct. 28, ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Tennessee Titans . Chase was in the locker room at the conclusion of practice and later was listed on the injury report as a non-participant for practice. Chase had five catches for 62 receiving yards with a touchdown in the team's Week 7 rout of the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Earlier in the month, Chase won appeals of fines for his "people's elbow" celebration . Two fines of $14,926 each for obscene gestures were rescinded from the team's NFL Week 2 win against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Chase made an impressive 45-yard touchdown catch from quarterback Joe Burrow during the third quarter of the team's NFL Week 5 win in Miami. Chase also made an absurd catch from Burrow for the first touchdown of the game against Houston. Jones drew a 15-yard penalty. Miller was not penalized, and wasn't fined by the league . CBS analyst Robert Turbin said he couldn't believe Miller didn't draw a flag. away.headline: Cowboys defenders Quinnen Williams, Caleb Downs added to injury report vs. Cardinals
away.blurb: Rookie defensive back Caleb Downs was limited in a walkthrough practice with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Quinnen Williams was also a new addition to the injury report as he's dealing with a hamstring injury. He was limited on Wednesday. FRISCO - The Cowboys added some new names to the injury report Wednesday. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Tuesday that there were a few players dealing with some minor injuries, but nothing significant. The Cowboys could also be on the verge of some players returning . Safety PJ Locke III (foot) and outside linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) were both full participants Wednesday. Locke was added to injured reserve after hurting his foot in the Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders. Liufau fractured his forearm in the preseason finale. The Cowboys created one roster spot earlier this week when they waived running back Emari Demercado. He was claimed by the Houston Texans on Wednesday. If the Cowboys activate both Locke and Liufau, they'll have to make one more roster move. Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson, another player on injured reserve , was seen working in the rehabilitation group during practice. He's been on injured reserve since he suffered a hamstring injury in late September. His practice window hasn't been opened yet. Read this story on dallasnews.com

away.headline: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love returns to practice before Cowboys clash
away.blurb: Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love returned to practice on a limited basis Wednesday ahead of the team’s Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys . Love has missed Arizona’s last two games because of an ankle injury that has troubled him since before the 2026 regular season began. The third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has an opportunity to return this week, although his participation in the remaining practices could determine his availability. The Cardinals have two more practices scheduled before releasing their official game statuses on Friday. Love’s potential return comes as the team manages an extensive injury report. Fifteen players appeared on Wednesday’s list, with nine unable to participate. Running back Tyler Allgeier (toe), safety Budda Baker (rest), linebacker Josh Sweat (rest), defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle) and offensive linemen Isaac Seumalo (rest), Elijah Wilkinson (knee) and Jon Gaines II (ankle) were among those sidelined. Zaven Collins (illness) and Mack Wilson Sr. (rest/knee) also missed practice. Quarterback Carson Beck (back), wide receiver Michael Wilson (ribs), cornerbacks Max Melton (knee) and Kei’Trel Clark (illness), and safety Andrew Wingard (knee) joined Love as limited participants. Michael Wilson wore a yellow non-contact jersey because of his sore ribs. Should Love be available Sunday, the Cardinals could distribute carries among all three backfield options. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Arizona has relied on Allgeier and Bam Knight during Love’s absence. In the Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos, Knight played 53% of the snaps compared with Allgeier’s 47%, finishing with 48 rushing yards on seven carries and adding three receptions for 15 yards. Across his first five NFL games, Love has recorded 245 rushing yards on 67 carries at 3.7 yards per attempt, along with 11 receptions for 36 yards and two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. away.headline: Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7
away.blurb: Love did not practice all last week and did not play against the Los Angeles Rams . He was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday. It sounds like he will sit the rest of this week as well. On Wednesday, coach Mike LaFleur indicated the Cardinals are focused on getting him right. "He's feeling better, but it kind of goes without saying — (We're) not going to put him out there until he feels 100%." Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7 Jess Root, Cardinals Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals do not expect to have rookie running back Jeremiyah Love back in Week 7. According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports , Love is expected to miss the Cardinals' game against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Love has been dealing with a lingering ankle injury for weeks. It is not the same ankle he sprained in the preseason. That ankle has healed, and he is not impacted by that. He has played in five games this season. He has rushed for 245 yards and a touchdown, averaging 3.7 yards per attempt. With no Love expected on Sunday, Tyler Allgeier will start and Bam Knight will play in Love's place. Knight rushed for 80 yards against the Rams in Week 6. Evan Hull will likely get elevated from the practice squad. Darius Robinson and Jon Gaines were added to an already lengthy list of Cardinals that featured Walter Nolen, Budda Baker and Jeremiyah Love among others. Cardinals Thursday Injury Report FULL : Isaac Seumalo (rest), Josh Sweat (rest), Jedrick Wills (illness), The Cardinals, hoping to again play the role of spoiler against Denver, could be massively shorthanded in making that happen as numerous stars are staring down a legitimate possibility of missing time. Baker, Love, Wingard and Nolen have all missed consecutive days of practice now for Arizona. With the Cardinals hoping to take advantage of a disfunctional Broncos offense, Arizona's defense needs all hands on deck. “Last few years. They’re very smart. They’re very well coached," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of the Broncos' defense. "I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them. You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it. "They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nolen, a second-year defensive lineman, has shown the ability to wreck offensive gameplans on a weekly basis. The one drawback? He's battled injuries since entering the league. Nolen suffered a calf injury before training camp of his rookie season, which saw him miss the beginning of 2025 before returning halfway through the year. He played a handful of games and showed massive promise before suffering a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve, ending his year. Nolen had surgery (later revealed to be a meniscus) but made a full recovery and was healthy for 2026's training camp, though he suffered a minor lower body injury during the team's time at State Farm Stadium. Last week was the first regular season game Nolen missed for this year. Nolen holds potential to be one of the best young defensive linemen in the NFL, and Arizona certainly needs it. Their defensive line pressure rate of 24.7% ranks dead-last in the league. In a front seven that's been largely uninspiring, Nolen's presence has been noticeable on a weekly basis. In six games this season, Nolen has 14 tackles, one sack and three quarterback hits. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. picks.blurb: Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers win World Series NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 27, 2026 at 2:38 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Minnesota Vikings plan their next massive blitz, the Detroit Lions ride the wave of a big division win. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFC North clash. It's a critical game for the Lions. The NFC North could end up with only two playoff teams. That's because the 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams still seem like firm bets. And that leaves only one other Wild Card spot. The Lions stand at 4-2 while the Vikings are 6-0. A loss would leave the Lions three games back of first place with nearly half the season in the rearview mirror. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will rush for 100-plus yards It's tough to throw against the Vikings. They rank No. 2 in the NFL against the pass, allowing just 155 yards per game. And while their run defense is good, it's still the better path to consistently moving the football. Gibbs is fourth in the NFL with 620 yards through six games. Look for the Lions to put a saddle on him against the Vikings. Yes, the Lions are clearly overusing Gibbs already. He's almost on a record pace , according to NBC Sports. "If Gibbs keeps to his current pace of 27.7 touches per game for the entire 17-game season, he'll finish this season with a whopping 470 touches," Michael David Smith wrote. "That would be the second-most in a season in NFL history, second only to former James Wilder, who had 492 touches with the 1984 Buccaneers." Gibbs should get close to that number of touches on the ground alone. He had 29 carries against the Saints and Packers this season. Look for the neighborhood of 25 against the Vikings. He's averaging 4.6 per carry, so that easily puts him over 100. And don't worry about the injury scare late against the Packers, according to mlive.com. During his postgame media session, Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Gibbs is OK and avoided serious injury . "Yeah, we got him checked," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "He should be good. That's that whole, 'Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game, or you just go score?' Sometimes I question that. I don't know, maybe we shouldn't just, but all good. It's a good win." Lions will double the Vikings' season average in points allowed For the season, the Vikings are allowing just 12.3 points per game. Over the last three games, they are giving up just 33 points. But the Lions will hit them for 24-plus points. Not only will Gibbs cut loose, but his runs will set up play-action daggers for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. This is no timid prediction. The Vikings defense is the real deal. The players will even tell you that , according to The Athletic. "It's a generational group," cornerback Isaiah Rodgers said. "We've got guys who go out and trust the scheme. They trust (Flores and his staff). The stats speak for themselves." Defensive tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez said it is togetherness that brings the good outcomes. "Hopefully, that showed the joy we have on the field with each other," Rodriguez said. "We want to work hard for each other. We want to be right." But the Lions are a different beast. They are king of the offensive jungle for a reason. They rank No. 2 in the NFL with 397.3 yards per game. The NFL used to be a league where great defense would pretty much always shut down a great offense. But the rules have changed. And the Lions will cut loose for a point total the Vikings haven't allowed since 22 in the season opener against the Packers. Vikings QB Kyler Murray will have his best game of the season For all the Lions are on offense, they ain't that on defense. They rank dead last in the league with 391 yards allowed per game. Murray hasn't thrown for 250 yards in a game yet this season. In fact, he hasn't done it since 2024. And he only has three touchdown passes in basically four games played. He missed almost all of the season opener after a first-quarter injury. But the Lions are relatively decent against the run. They are an open gate against the pass. And Murray will take advantage with some chunk plays down the field. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is standing behind Murray, according to The Athletic. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far-off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." One reason for optimism is that Murray has gotten better at play action. The Vikings used play action on nearly half of Murray's dropbacks in Week 7. And Murray hit on eight of 11 passes. There's still hope for Murray. Some people have been writing him off and saying the Vikings should move on, but this is a chance for him to silence critics. picks.blurb: 1. Defense wins championships, but will it win this game? The Lions and Vikings couldn't be more opposite at this point in the season. Minnesota is winning with defense, and Detroit is getting by with an electric offense. So it'll be strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness in this key NFC North clash. 2. Not-so smooth sailing: The Vikings are about to enter some rough waters when the calendar flips to November. Minnesota cleaned up with wins over the Saints , Dolphins and Colts in October, but the schedule's difficulty is about to be turned up a notch. The Lions, Bills, Packers and Niners await in the penultimate month of the year for the last undefeated team. We're about to find out if the Vikings are a contender or pretender. 3. Scoring drought: For the first time this season, Jahmyr Gibbs didn't get into the end zone. For someone who has his eyes on LaDainian Tomlinson's record of 31, that drought can't last much longer. Gibbs has nine total touchdowns through six games, but he'll still have to pick up the pace. That watch continues into Week 8. Lions vs Vikings odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -4.5 Moneyline: Lions -218; Vikings +180 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions vs Vikings USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Vikings keep winning, and their defense keeps making everybody miserable. That travels. But the Lions present a much tougher offensive assignment than the Colts, especially with Jahmyr Gibbs creating problems as both a runner and receiver. Detroit's best approach is keeping Jared Goff out of obvious passing situations, where Brian Flores can turn an ordinary Sunday into an escape room. Minnesota's historically bad offense remains the concern. Can it consistently hold up its end against a team capable of sustaining drives? I'm expecting a tight, physical division game, with the Lions bouncing back to produce just enough offense to hand the Vikings their first loss. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 20, Vikings 13 This might be the end of the line for the Vikings' undefeated run. While Brian Flores' vise-grip defense gives Minnesota a chance in any contest, it will be exceedingly difficult if the Kyler Murray-led offense remains out of sync. Deroit's defense isn't inspiring fear in anyone, but Brian Branch's return has helped the unit at least approach reliability. Jared Goff has the third-highest passer rating of any quarterback against the blitz this year, so Flores might have to be particularly creative in how he tries to box in the Lions' attack. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Lions 21, Vikings 17 Unstoppable force meets immovable object. The Lions defense couldn't catch a cold this season, and the Vikings offense appears to be doing their best to boost Brian Flores' chances of landing a head coaching job this offseason. If you like chaos, this Flores defense is for you. Physical and blitz-heavy, Minnesota is the last unbeaten team solely because of that unit. However, it's hard to have any faith in the Kyler Murray-led unit on the other side of the ball. This figures to be an ugly NFC North contest. Trust the Lions' offense to eke out a win at home. away.headline: Vikings get positive injury update on RB Aaron Jones: report
away.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions. away.blurb: Though safety Kerby Joseph made his long-awaited practice return on Wednesday, a number of other Lions stars didn't practice for a variety of reasons. Lions head coach Dan Campbell had said earlier in the day that Detroit was planning to hold some players out. "St.'s doing good, Ennis (Rakestraw Jr.) is doing good. Going to hold them out of practice. We're going to do a walkthrough, and then roll right into practice for a little bit here. So, just kinda, it goes all-in-one. I think those guys will be at walkthrough, but I don't see them out there during the practice portion. I'm going to hold a couple of other guys back just to get them off their feet, but they'll be at walkthrough," Campbell said. But, star running back Jahmyr Gibbs also didn't practice and was listed with a shoulder injury. Fellow running back Jacob Saylors (neck) was a limited participant. Like Campbell said, Amon-Ra St. Brown sat out with his ankle injury, and Rakestraw was a limited participant. Starting defensive lineman Tyleik Williams also didn't practice due to illness. Starting right tackle Brian O'Neill was a limited participant with a knee injury. As Campbell suggested, Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Alim McNeill, and Penei Sewell didn't practice as a scheduled rest day. away.headline: Detroit Lions sign former Vikings DL to practice squad, release WR
away.blurb: Originally an undrafted free agent by the Vikings in 2024 out of Oregon , Taimani finished with 22 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one quarterback hurry, and one fumble recovery during the 2023 college football season with the Ducks. As Sunday's NFC North showdown approaches, the Detroit Lions (4-2) signed former Minnesota Vikings (6-0) defensive lineman Taki Taimani to their practice squad on Tuesday. Taimani, a 6-foot-1, 309-pound lineman, has appeared in nine NFL games (all with the Vikings ) and has registered four tackles. Per Pro Football Focus , Taimani logged 70 defensive snaps in 2024 and carded a 61.2 overall defensive grade that season. In 2025, Taimani tallied just 35 defensive snaps and had an overall defensive grade of 27.4 last season from PFF . In its corresponding move, the Lions released wide receiver Lawrence Keys from their practice squad. Detroit signed Keys back in June after a stint in the UFL with the Houston Gamblers. The 5-foot-11, 170-pound receiver finished second in the UFL with 1,001 all-purpose yards over the Gamblers' 10-game schedule. Keys registered 349 receiving yards on 24 receptions including two touchdown catches. The 26-year-old also returned 19 kickoffs for 518 yards and 11 punts for 134 yards and a 12.2 average, which ranked third in the league. After going undrafted in 2024, Keys signed with the Buffalo Bills . But, he was released prior to the start of the 2024 NFL season. During his college career at Notre Dame and then Tulane, Keys caught 81 passes for 1,080 yards and nine touchdowns. Keys' most productive collegiate season was 2023 when he hauled in 30 passes for 296 yards and two scores. Keys was waived by the Lions in August during training camp with an injury settlement before signing back onto the practice squad in late September. home.headline: Detroit Lions sign former Vikings DL to practice squad, release WR
home.blurb: Originally an undrafted free agent by the Vikings in 2024 out of Oregon , Taimani finished with 22 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one quarterback hurry, and one fumble recovery during the 2023 college football season with the Ducks. As Sunday's NFC North showdown approaches, the Detroit Lions (4-2) signed former Minnesota Vikings (6-0) defensive lineman Taki Taimani to their practice squad on Tuesday. Taimani, a 6-foot-1, 309-pound lineman, has appeared in nine NFL games (all with the Vikings ) and has registered four tackles. Per Pro Football Focus , Taimani logged 70 defensive snaps in 2024 and carded a 61.2 overall defensive grade that season. In 2025, Taimani tallied just 35 defensive snaps and had an overall defensive grade of 27.4 last season from PFF . In its corresponding move, the Lions released wide receiver Lawrence Keys from their practice squad. Detroit signed Keys back in June after a stint in the UFL with the Houston Gamblers. The 5-foot-11, 170-pound receiver finished second in the UFL with 1,001 all-purpose yards over the Gamblers' 10-game schedule. Keys registered 349 receiving yards on 24 receptions including two touchdown catches. The 26-year-old also returned 19 kickoffs for 518 yards and 11 punts for 134 yards and a 12.2 average, which ranked third in the league. After going undrafted in 2024, Keys signed with the Buffalo Bills . But, he was released prior to the start of the 2024 NFL season. During his college career at Notre Dame and then Tulane, Keys caught 81 passes for 1,080 yards and nine touchdowns. Keys' most productive collegiate season was 2023 when he hauled in 30 passes for 296 yards and two scores. Keys was waived by the Lions in August during training camp with an injury settlement before signing back onto the practice squad in late September. Last week the Jets lost a hard fought game to the defending AFC champions New England Patriots. That was understandable. Much less understandable was today's 28 – 25 loss at home to the previously winless Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins dominated the action for most of the game, building a two touchdown lead at halftime and maintaining an 11 point lead with less than five minutes remaining in the game before a late Jets touchdown made the score look closer than the game actually was. This loss came against a Dolphins team that had never held a lead at any point in the season prior to today. Today the Dolphins never trailed. It was a humiliating performance by the Jets. The horrendous Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-5 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Now the Jets look to get back on the winning track as they stay home to take on the 3-4 Las Vegas Raiders in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Raiders have lost four straight games after starting the season 3-0. Their latest loss came at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams by a 35 – 21 score. The Raiders' defense has collapsed in their four game losing streak, surrendering 30+ points in each of the four games. With the Raiders making the long trip east for this game and suffering through the early game start, on paper this looks like a get well game for the Jets. However, the way the Jets are playing no game on the schedule should be looked at as an easy win. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . picks.blurb: 1. Klint Kubiak vowed there was "no controversy" at quarterback, where Kirk Cousins will remain the starter. While the 38-year-old might have hit a wall last week in trying to navigate the Rams ' relentless blitzes, the NFL's leading passer is hardly the Silver and Black's biggest problem. Kubiak has bemoaned an inert running game that has left Las Vegas needing to sling its way back into games. It could be tricky to get things going against a Jets defense that ranks fifth in defensive EPA per rush. 2. Can New York finally get Garrett Wilson involved early and often in the offensive game plan? One week after he was essentially a non-factor against the Patriots, Wilson was held without a reception or target in the first half against a woefully undermanned Dolphins secondary. Wilson and Glenn both downplayed the wideout's heated confrontation with quarterback Geno Smith, but expect feeding the receiver early and often to be a point of emphasis for Gang Green. 3. How the Raiders' defense handles the Jets' ground game could determine the course of the game. The Silver and Black allowed a season-high 199 rushing yards to the Rams last week, with a vulnerability that has been apparent all season finally reaching critical mass. New York, meanwhile, has seen Braelon Allen eclipse 100 rushing yards in two of the last three games he's handled as Breece Hall's fill-in. Jets vs Raiders odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Jets -1.5 Moneyline: Jets -125; Raiders +105 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Jets vs Raiders USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Jets 24, Raiders 21 Welcome back to Narrative Street! Geno Smith gets his former team, while Kirk Cousins keeps the Raiders' starting job despite the growing curiosity about Fernando Mendoza. Neither team has earned much trust lately, so let's acknowledge that before pretending this is an easy handicap. Smith threw three touchdowns against Miami, and Las Vegas' defense offers an opportunity for another productive afternoon. The Raiders need more from their running game to keep Cousins from carrying every possession. I'm giving New York the slightest edge at the Meadowlands, and a fifth straight loss for Las Vegas. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Jets 24, Raiders 20 This game could end up shaping the second half of the season for two coaching staffs that seem to be at a crossroads. The Jets' secondary might not be able to mug the Raiders' receiving corps the way that the Patriots and Rams did, but the pass rush should be able to generate sufficient heat to keep Kirk Cousins out of sorts. Las Vegas seems desperate to find any semblance of offensive balance - as well as some stops against the run - but a breakthrough might not materialize this week. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Raiders 26, Jets 20 You can put a bow on the 2026 Jets. The season, and maybe the Aaron Glenn era, came to an end with a loss to the Dolphins in Week 7. It's going to be a bumpy ride to the finish, but there is no doubt the destination is a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That's why it's fitting that New York will get a glimpse at what it could've had last season. Fernando Mendoza won't play, but it's the idea he's wearing silver and black that sticks. The Raiders are just better. Vegas gets back on track. Tonka Hemingway and Quay Walker participated in practice on a limited basis on Thursday. When asked if running back Mike Washington earned more reps, Kubiak stated, "Yes," he had. Washington was listed on the injury report as a limited participant on Wednesday and did not practice on Thursday afternoon. This could be bad news for the Raiders. Or it could be precautionary, since Bowers missed Friday's practice before his first start of the season, and Jeanty did not practice late in Week 5 before Las Vegas faced the New England Patriots, but he still played that Sunday . Washington averaged about five carries per game before last Sunday. Heading into Week 6, Jeanty averaged nearly 18 carries per game before that number was cut in half last Sunday, as Washington carried the ball double his season average per game. If Washington is out on Sunday against the Rams , Jeanty's health and durability will be tested.
