away.headline: NFL Week 7 Injury Report: Raiders' Quay Walker and Rams' Puka Nacua Listed
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders linebacker Quay Walker has been downgraded to questionable with a chest injury ahead of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. The change raises uncertainty about his availability for the Week 7 matchup at Allegiant Stadium. ESPN's Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden reported the downgrade on X on Saturday. Walker had been a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the Raiders' official injury report. The injury report also lists running back Mike Washington Jr. as questionable for Las Vegas with foot and back issues. For Los Angeles, wide receiver Puka Nacua is questionable with a calf injury, while linebacker Nate Landman has been ruled out with a concussion. Walker was limited during the first two practices of the week before completing Friday's session without a game-status designation on the team's published report. The subsequent downgrade means his availability remains uncertain, although the available reporting does not establish whether he experienced a setback or explain the reason for the change. The Raiders host the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. Las Vegas will need to clarify Walker's status before the game, while his questionable designation leaves open the possibility that he could still play. His potential absence would give Las Vegas another defensive issue to assess before facing a Rams team that enters Week 7 at 2-4, fourth in the NFC West. home.headline: New York Jets Add David Bailey, Braelon Allen to Injury Report
home.blurb: The latest addition is star rookie edge rusher David Bailey, who has a groin injury that is keeping him out of practice on Wednesday. Bailey sustained the injury against the Dolphins, but finished the game. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Bailey came to the Jets practice facility on Monday and said his groin injury was still bothering him. Glenn declined to speculate on whether the injury would keep Bailey out of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. "We'll see how he operates," the coach said. "We'll see during the week." Bailey did not practice on Wednesday, with Glenn waiting until later in the week to make an official game status designation. Of greater concern may be the absence of defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat. The biggest player in the NFL, Sweat sustained a knee injury against the Dolphins and is listed as doubtful. Also doubtful for the Raiders game is edge Joseph Ossai, who has an ankle injury. Both are considered week-to-week on availability. Also nursing an ankle is running back Braelon Allen, who ran for more than 100 yards against the Dolphins. He was listed as limited for Wednesday's practice. The Jets' other star running back, Breece Hall, may return against the Raiders after being a game-time no-go against the Dolphins. He has 357 yards since Hall went down in Week 3, and has performed so well that the Jets are trying to scheme a way to have both backs on the field at the same time. Bailey has been a force for the Jets in his rookie season. Bailey and Pro Football Hall of Famer Brian Urlacher are the only players since 2000 to have at least 5 1/2 sacks and 35 tackles in their first seven NFL games. Allen ran for 104 yards on 17 carries against the Dolphins and set a career high with six receptions. "I think you know that Braelon, we also gave him the ball when Breece was with us and playing," Glenn said. "So, I've said this here numerous times: Both of those guys can carry the load. home.headline: Dolphins’ Caleb Douglas cleared to return from ankle injury against Jets
home.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. After linebacker Willie Gay Jr. popped up on the Thursday injury report due to illness, Hafley said he’s back in the building Friday and feeling better. Gay participated in practice and is deemed questionable to play. The Dolphins have defensive end Rob Beal Jr., who has been back at practice through his hamstring injury, doubtful. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who has hurt quadriceps, is out. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Questionable, along with Hall, are running back Kene Nwangwu (knee) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Florida & Caribbean Experiences Florida Jewish Journal Florida Jewish Journal Branded Content Paid Partner Content MIAMI GARDENS — Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas is cleared to play in the upcoming game against the New York Jets on Sunday. Before Friday’s practice, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas will be good to go after missing three games with an ankle injury. The team’s injury report listed Douglas free of any game status designation after he underwent a full practice session. On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. He hadn't played in a while. … It brings us some extra juice.” Without him, the Miami passing offense ranks 31st among 32 teams in the league on the year. The 6-foot-4 target who led the team with 94 receiving yards in the team’s opener against the Las Vegas Raiders could provide a boost to the passing game. Hafley also said running back Jaylen Wright, who has been dealing with a nagging foot injury, will play. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton No one predicted the Browns (5-2) would be tied for first in the AFC North heading into Week 8 of the NFL season, but here they sit as they prepare to play the Steelers (5-2) in Pittsburgh this Sunday. Cleveland has won five of its last six after beating Tennessee 27-24 last Sunday, while Pittsburgh enters on a three-game winning streak following a 16-10 victory over New Orleans in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris. The matchup also comes only a month after Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 on October 1. Last week, Cleveland again showed an ability to win late in their game against Tennessee. After falling behind 14-0 in the first quarter, the Browns rallied behind Quinshon Judkins , who rushed for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion , who caught eight passes for 129 yards. Deshaun Watson delivered perhaps his best performance of the season, completing 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards while adding a nine-yard rushing touchdown. After Tennessee tied the game with 58 seconds remaining, Watson immediately answered, hitting Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards to help set up Andre Szmyt’s game-winning 32-yard field goal as time expired. It was Watson’s fifth fourth-quarter winning drive of the season. Pittsburgh’s latest win was less dramatic but built around the combination it hopes can carry them to a division title and a playoff berth: Aaron Rodgers , an effective running game and a defense capable of closing out tight games. Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans, including a four-yard score to Darnell Washington that gave him 540 career touchdown passes and moved him past Peyton Manning into third place in NFL history. Jaylen Warren supplied 101 rushing yards on 18 carries. The Pittsburgh defense held the Saints to just 18 rushing yards and Payton Wilson produced a red-zone interception. The biggest storyline may simply be whether Pittsburgh can reverse what happened in Cleveland four weeks earlier. In that Oct. 1 meeting, the Browns built a 21-7 advantage before Rodgers led a fourth-quarter comeback, eventually tying the game at 24 on his three-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth and ensuing two-point run. Watson then went 4-for-5 for 46 yards on Cleveland’s final drive, positioning Szmyt for a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining to give the Browns a 27-24 victory. Watson finished with 268 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice; DK Metcalf added 115 receiving yards and Warren ran for 93. That first meeting established the template for Sunday: division rivals comfortable playing close games led by veteran quarterbacks who have repeatedly delivered late, and a Browns team trying to complete an improbable season sweep against a Steelers club returning home looking to reclaim the upper hand in the AFC North. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. Cleveland ranks 27th in touchdown percentage (3.1%), 28th in points scored (19.0 per game), 30th in third-down conversion rate (32.58%), and 32nd in sack rate allowed (11.85%) with 25 sacks taken, most in the NFL. away.blurb: For the Steelers, it would only be a mild surprise for them to be sitting in that position. Cleveland, however, has been one of the big surprises of the NFL season. They haven't exactly dominated any of their opponents, and the offense is still extremely limited by the play of quarterback DeShaun Watson. For the Steelers to win their rematch with the Browns in Week 8, they will need to continue to dominate their opponents in both trenches . Pittsburgh has out-rushed their opponents 364 to 186 over their three-game win streak, forcing their opponents to try to beat them through the air. Even though he has been better this season compared to the majority of his Browns career prior, DeShaun Watson is still a limited QB who can't carry the load. If Pittsburgh can make Cleveland one-dimensional offensively, they should be able to easily take care of them at home. How will the way this game plays out affect both team's trade deadline approach? Let me get this out of the way to start: I don't think either of these teams should be buyers at the trade deadline. The Browns are way ahead of schedule, but they still don't have a plan at QB long term and have been killing the draft over the past few years. They should sit on their hands and see how far they can go this season with what they have. For the Steelers, the story is similar. Once Aaron Rodgers retires after the season, their QB job will be wide open yet again. As much as they may want to go all-in during Rodgers' last hurrah, there aren't any players who will be available who would truly move the needle. Sure, you could add a receiver or corner that might give you a reasonable boost. But to what end? Regardless of what I think, though, I have to imagine that the Steelers will look for reinforcements no matter how the game plays out. The Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cleveland Browns will face off in Week 8 under very rare circumstances. The two teams have matching 5-2 records thus far, and the winner of this game will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. away.blurb: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return Skip to main content SI.COM The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. Michael Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Out Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game. Dillon Gabriel, Teven Jenkins, Out Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line. If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2. The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. Pittsburgh Steelers veteran safety DeShon Elliott was trending in the right direction at practice throughout the week. The team took the last step for Elliott to make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the New Orleans Saints . On Saturday, the Steelers announced they have activated Elliott from the reserve/injured list. He will be eligible to play Sunday against the Saints in the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Paris, France. Elliott fully practiced Wednesday and Thursday before the team flew to Europe. The Steelers then canceled their Friday practice in France. The veteran safety doesn't have a designation on the team's injury report. Barring a last-minute setback, Elliott will dress for the first time this season versus the Saints. On Wednesday, the Steelers released safety Rayshawn Jenkins. The team didn't make a corresponding move, which left open a roster spot for Elliott on Saturday. Elliott started this season on the PUP list because of a knee injury he sustained last season. Elliott hyperextended his knee, which required surgery, in Week 8 almost exactly a year ago on October 26. Steelers Activate DeShon Elliott for Week 7 The Jenkins release was a pretty strong giveaway that Elliott would play in Week 7. The Steelers moved on from the safety suddenly even though they later placed defensive tackle Sebastian Joseph-Day on injured reserve. Elliott will be the third for the game against the Saints. Elliott is likely to start the contest. He started 19 of 20 games from 2024-25 with the Steelers before his season-ending injury last year. In five games during 2025, Elliott posted 38 combined tackles. He also had one tackle for loss, three quarterback hits, one sack, two pass defenses and one interception. Elliott began his career in the AFC North with the Baltimore Ravens . He spent three seasons with the Ravens, where he became a regular starter in 2020. Since then, he's only not started on two occasions while being on the active roster. In 2022 and 2023, Elliott played for the Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins . The safety signed with the Steelers during the 2024 offseason. Steelers Safety Depth for Saints Matchup But rookie Robert Spears-Jennings has played well in the veteran's absence. Spears- Jennings has played at least 53% of the team's defensive snaps the past three weeks. The rookie lined up for a season-high 47 snaps (63.5%) last Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . away.blurb: Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson, LB Divine Deablo ruled out vs. 49ers Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Atlanta has several key players who are questionable for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. That includes the Atlanta Falcons and San Francisco 49ers, who each enter Sunday's game with availability questions for key players. Atlanta's injury report has been lengthy all week long, but it includes a few players who could be making a return in Week 7. Most notably are cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson. Their return would bolster a secondary that has been dinged up in recent weeks but was playing well at the start of the season. If Terrell, who has been on injured reserve for the last four games, and Henderson do return, that could afford a bit of flexibility in the secondary, especially with slot cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. ruled out for Sunday due to a hamstring injury he sustained late in Week 6. Bowman is one of four players ruled out against the 49ers. The others are linebacker Divine Deablo, offensive tackle Michael Jerrell and running back Brian Robinson Jr., the latter two of whom first appeared on Wednesday's injury report as limited participants with bicep and hamstring injuries, respectively. Deablo has been the key communicator for Atlanta's defense this season, but the team feels confident that rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable for the game with a neck injury , can step up in that area if needed. The Falcons had three players begin practicing this week after spending time on injured reserve. While those three players—wide receiver Beaux Collins, offensive lineman Cameron Williams and Terrell—are listed as questionable for the game, they would need to be added to Atlanta's active roster by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to play on Sunday. home.headline: Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield back, rule out three starters
home.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game looking to rebound from a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay reason to be optimistic, but the absences of Egbuka, Goedeke, and Winfield will force the team to adjust on both sides of the ball. home.blurb: Mayfield, who has missed the last three games after dislocating his right thumb in Week 3, continues to make progress toward a potential return. The veteran quarterback was a full participant Wednesday and Thursday, providing optimism that he could be back under center when Tampa Bay travels to Carolina. Elsewhere on the injury report, running back Bucky Irving (illness) and cornerback Zyon McCollum (illness) were upgraded to limited participation after sitting out Wednesday. Defensive tackle Calijah Kancey (illness) also improved to full participation. However, wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf), and linebacker Christian Rozeboom (finger) remained sidelined for a second consecutive day. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. was also held out for rest. For Carolina, outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and Thomas Incoom (calf) remained out of practice Thursday. Running back Chuba Hubbard, linebacker Devin Lloyd, offensive tackle Taylor Moton, and tight end Darren Waller all returned as full participants after receiving rest Wednesday. Thus far, they locked up long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Travon Walker, cornerback Montaric Brown, and tight end Brenton Strange, so you could make the case that general manager James Gladstone achieved the goal. That said, Parker Washington is still waiting on an extension. A sixth-round pick in 2023, Washington showed flashed his first two seasons but was stucked behind Christian Kirk. Jacksonville paved the way for him to start when Kirk was traded to the Houston Texans. Right off the bat, Washington became a key contributor on offense, registering 58 receptions for 807 yards with five touchdowns, all career bests, last year. Washington wasted no time picking up where he left off last year, racking up 26 receptions for 416 yards with four touchdowns. The former Penn State Nittany Lion is on pace to register the first 1,000-yard season of his career and should have no trouble getting the top-market contract he's been looking for . Although the Jags reportedly offered Washington $25 million per year before Week 1 , he rejected the offer. It's possible that he's aiming for an annual average of $30 million. Based on his production, he may be able to get it, and he'll have a prime opportunity when he plays the Colts. Already, Washington posted his first 100-yard game of the season against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. He'll get his second one in Week 8 when he registers seven receptions for a monster 140 yards with two touchdowns against Indy. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
away.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. But the Jaguars drafted Huskey for situations like this, and it is time to let him play. With that said, there was some good news for the Jaguars on the injury front. Cornerback Montaric Brown was a full participant after missing time with a hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all but six snaps in the Jaguars' last three games. Brown was struggling at times before his injury, but a healthy Brown would help change the math in the cornerback room and potentially allow the Jaguars to play Jarrian Jones in the slot more than he has played since Brown started missing practice and game reps due to injury. home.headline: Vega Ioane's injury could give Jaguars' D-line a sudden edge against Ravens
home.blurb: Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Ioane suffered an MCL sprain, adding that he'll miss time even though it's a short-term injury. The rookie hog molly left the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and didn't return. It's hard to tell just how much time is a little time, but if it wasn't serious, Ioane would be week-to-week or questionable for Week 8. He's not, meaning that there's a strong chance he won't suit up against Jacksonville. Following their BYE, the Jacksonville Jaguars will face the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8 . And after their AFC showdown, they'll face off against the Baltimore Ravens. While it's hard to tell if Lamar Jackson will suit up for the game — he's seemingly dealing with a high-ankle sprain — the Jags now know that they probably won't have to face rookie offensive guard Vega Ioane. The Jaguars may not have to worry about Vega Ioane when they play the Ravens The Jaguars will face Baltimore in Week 9. It will be a Thursday Night game. Given that there's a three-day gap between Sunday games and Thursday, players who don't suit up Sunday often miss the Thursday bout. That doesn't bode well for Vega Ioane's availability. A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2026, Ioane got off to a strong start to his rookie season, giving up just one sack and eight total pressures in six games. Ioane began the season at right guard but eventually moved to center. He returned to right guard when Baltimore traded for Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles. Emery Jones Jr. may be the next man up. You may also like: AFC South Week 8 power ranking: The Jags win big without playing The Jaguars' D-Line must take advantage of Vega Ioane's absence Lamar Jackson has missed three games with injuries . Tyler Huntley has filled in for him, throwing for 664 yards with four touchdowns and one interception during his absence. There hasn't been that steep a drop-off at quarterback, but without Vega Ioane, the Baltimore offensive line could have trouble protecting whoever lines up behind center. This is encouraging news for a Jacksonville defensive line that has struggled to create pressure from the interior. While the Jaguars excel at stuffing the run, they have had trouble getting after the quarterback this season, registering just 11 sacks. Sure, they've racked up pressures, but those haven't always translated into big plays, takeaways, and such. Maybe the Jags can get better production from their interior defensive line after their break. Arik Armstead has played at a high level at times but has been inconsistent. On the other hand, DaVon Hamilton won't offer much in the pass-rush department, while Ruke Orhorhoro hasn't made the leap he was expected to make when he was traded to Jacksonville. Rookie Albert Regis is also in the mix but has barely played. When you add it all up, it's easy to see why the Jaguars are being urged to trade for a defensive tackle . Maybe they will, maybe they won't, but they'll at least get a bit of a break when they play the Rave

home.headline: Jaguars Get Devastating Injury Update On Left Tackle Anton Harrison
home.blurb: my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores National Football League Add FOX Sports on Google Jaguars Get Devastating Injury Update On Left Tackle Anton Harrison Published Oct. 23, 2026 1:01 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the remainder of the season after tearing a ligament in his right knee. Harrison injured his knee during a win against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Oct. 11. He spun on the field turf to make a block and twisted his knee when he planted his right leg. Harrison was carted to the locker room. Harrison waited until the Jaguars (4-2) returned from two weeks overseas to have arthroscopic surgery to determine the extent of the damage. The scope Wednesday revealed a torn anterior cruciate ligament. Jacksonville already placed Harrison on injured reserve. Backup Walker Little, who has started 40 games over six seasons with Jacksonville, is expected to replace Harrison in the lineup the rest of the season. Harrison has started 53 games for the Jaguars since they selected him 27th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. The former Oklahoma Sooners standout moved from right tackle to left tackle this season in hopes of improving Jacksonville’s run game, which ranks 14th this season, up from 20th in 2025. Harrison is Jacksonville's first starter to sustain a season-ending injury in 2026. Reporting by The Associated Press. home.headline: Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams
home.blurb: Myles Garrett has not played for the Los Angeles Rams since Week 1 and the team still is not sure if the edge rusher will return to the field any time soon. Sean McVay was asked about Garrett returning for the Los Angeles Chargers game on Sunday, and the head coach said that he wasn't sure if L.A.'s superstar offseason acquisition would practice this week or not. McVay was asked about both Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson potentially making a return to practice this week, but answered that he wasn't prepared to answer yet. The longer Garrett doesn't suit up, the harder it will be for the Rams to stay afloat in a tough 2026 season where the Rams need to go on a run to make Garrett's return worth it from a playoff perspective. By the time Garrett is ready, if he's ready, will there be a point to playing this season? Or, will it better to wait for 2027? Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams Danny Stone Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:41 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads McVay said he needs to meet with Reggie Scott, the Rams' Senior Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance, before he makes any type of determination. "I'm not sure yet. I'm not decided on those things." A follow-up question was asked with regard to when McVay would know whether or not either player would practice this week. McVay only offers further that he'll meet with the medical team and go from there. McVay doesn't offer any insight to how he thinks that meeting will go, just that he needs to meet with them before making a decision. "Once I get with Reggie and talk about the approach for the week. Then we'll just kinda follow their guidance based on where he's at and how he's feeling." It could be gamesmanship, it could be McVay wanted to have genuine deniability for this presser about whether Garrett will play this week or not, but at some point the team will need to make a decision on Garrett. And hopefully soon because the team invested a lot into him as an addition for a defense that is lacking serious firepower upfront this season. The Rams traded a first-round pick, Jared Verse, and more to to get Garrett . He hasn't played in a game since Week 1, as the 2025 sack leader has yet to notch one single sack or tackle for his new team. As McVay might say, "I'm not sure yet. I'm not decided on those things."

(Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian St. Clair Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The first game of the 2026 season for your Denver Broncos did not go according to plan. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Kansas City : Sixth in total offense (380.5 yards per game), fifth in rushing offense (141.5 YPG), 11th in passing offense (239.0 YPG), 14th in scoring offense (23.8 points per game). Denver : Thirtieth in total offense (270.0 yards per game), 24th in rushing offense (94.9 YPG), 27th in passing offense (175.1 YPG), tied for 24th in scoring offense (20.6 points per game). Defensive Rankings Kansas City : Fourteenth in total defense (323.3 yards per game), 13th in rushing defense (99.5 YPG), 17th in passing defense (223.8 YPG), second in scoring defense (17.2 points per game). Denver : Twenty-third in total defense (349.0 yards per game), 28th in rushing defense (133.3 YPG), 12th in passing defense (215.7 YPG), seventh in scoring defense (20.1 points per game). Here are the MHR staff's keys to Sunday's game. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Win the turnover battle on Sunday, and the Broncos put themselves in a great spot to win the game. — Ian St. Clair Stop the Chiefs run game Mahomes is continuing to play based off who he was two years ago and not putting in the effort to stay great. I like our chances if we force him to throw on our excellent secondary. Stop Kenneth Walker and win the game. — Sadaraine Tackle Kenneth Walker III The Broncos were hanging tough in the first half in that Week 1 matchup, but the horrific tackling eventually led to big plays in the run game. The Chiefs ran away from Denver in the second half. We all remember how much we overreacted to that first game, but man, did they miss too many tackles to count, and the overreaction was warranted. Since then, however, the Broncos defense has been pretty damn good and the offense is finally waking up. Keep up that momentum, and they should take care of business this weekend. — Tim Lynch Feed Jonah Coleman No need to get cute. Let Jonah Coleman build off the game he had against the Arizona Cardinals. Commit to the running attack. Get the young guys involved. Coleman and RJ Harvey had great games in Phoenix. Keep that going. The passing attack will open up once teams are forced to respect the run. — Adam Malnati Score more points than KC Using advanced analytics, the keys to this game are simple. When the Broncos score fewer points than their opponent, they are 0-2, and when they score more, they are 5-0. Further proving this point, they are 0-1 vs. the Chiefs this season when scoring fewer points than them. However, they were 2-0 against the Chiefs last season when they scored more points than their division rivals. So, according to these advanced analytics, if they can score more points than the Chiefs in this game, they will be 6-2. — Scotty Payne What are your keys to Sunday's game?

picks.blurb: 1. With Kenneth Walker III coming to town, the Broncos will be called on to clean up an operation that missed 28 tackles in the Chiefs' season-opening romp. Kansas City surely wants to get the Super Bowl 60 MVP back to his early-season form after the Seahawks kept him in check. Denver has shown signs in recent weeks of its run defense coalescing, but Sunday will mark a stiff test after the group overwhelmed shorthanded backfields in the last two weeks. 2. Injuries loom large in the matchup between the Chiefs' aerial attack and the Broncos' vaunted pass defense. Getting receiver Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore back could provide a significant boost to a Kansas City attack coming off arguably the worst offensive outing of Patrick Mahomes' tenure. But Denver could also get significant reinforcements with cornerback Patrick Surtain II trying to play after sitting out three weeks with an ankle injury. 3. A methodical Denver offense finally found its explosive streak last week against Arizona, with Bo Nix and RJ Harvey both reeling off long touchdowns. Repeating that effort against the Chiefs could be difficult, especially with Jaylen Waddle's status in question after he suffered a chest injury late against Arizona. But the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who had 93 rushing yards in his first game back from injured reserve, could help the Broncos avoid the obvious passing situations that plagued the team early in the season. The Broncos have won three straight, but their injury picture matters, particularly with Patrick Surtain II and Jaylen Waddle. The Chiefs have their own issues to sort through, and the Week 1 blowout doesn't tell us how this rematch will unfold. We should get a considerably tighter game, with both defenses making the offenses work. I'm not sure I trust Patrick Mahomes, given the lack of quality pass-catchers around him, but I do trust Kenneth Walker III against one of the NFL's worst run defenses on the heels of a homecoming dud. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Chiefs 17, Broncos 10 Even with all of their readily evident limitations, it's hard to believe the Chiefs could turn up truly putrid offensive performances in back-to-back weeks. Denver, on the other hand, might be dealing with its own regression to the mean, as it seems unlikely that last week's explosive plays will carry over against the Chiefs. A rout similar to Week 1 might not be in the cards, but Kansas City should be able to escape with the sweep. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Broncos 20, Chiefs 16 This should be a marquee game, but now it feels like just another game on the Sunday slate – due in part to a sleep-inducing Broncos' offense and very flawed Chiefs team. Kansas City's Week 1 blowout victory over Denver feels like a lifetime ago, and maybe that's because it was. Bo Nix showed some signs of life last week, while Patrick Mahomes is running out of receivers. If the Chiefs can't win by handing the ball off to Kenneth Walker III, they can't win. Denver knows that. We know that. The home team wins in the Mile High City. away.headline: Chiefs Week 7 injury report vs. Seahawks: Josh Simmons IR move throws wrinkle into KC offense
away.blurb: The distinction is that Simmons’ absence is not new. His IR placement instead eliminates the possibility of an immediate return, forcing Kansas City to keep building around its replacement personnel. For the offense, that makes this a sustained adjustment rather than a temporary bridge to an imminent return. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will continue at left tackle, while Joshua Ezeudu is expected to replace Moore on the right side against Seattle. The concern is the combined exposure at both edges. Helping one tackle with a tight end or running back can be manageable. Providing assistance on both sides can reduce the number of receivers available downfield. Moore missed every practice this week and is out with a concussion. Rice also recorded three consecutive nonparticipation listings before being ruled out with hamstring and knee injuries. Smith is out as well, with reporting identifying his injury as a hamstring issue. His absence further reduces the available offensive options. Travis Kelce offers reassurance. Despite limited participation throughout the week because of an ankle injury, he carries no game designation. That is different from being questionable, although it does not establish that he feels completely unrestricted. Defensively, L’Jarius Sneed is questionable after three limited practices with a knee injury. Chamarri Conner practiced fully throughout the week with a knee issue, while linebacker Cooper McDonald remained limited. Neither received a game designation. The central offensive issue remains protection. Simmons’ IR move does not suddenly dismantle a functioning lineup, but it extends reliance on replacements. With Moore and Rice also unavailable, Kansas City must pair sound blocking adjustments with efficient execution rather than expect Mahomes to solve every problem himself. home.headline: Broncos' Most Surprising Trade Candidate Is Hiding in Plain Sight
home.blurb: In the NFL, it's good not to be predictable. The Broncos have to make the tough decision to continue ceding snaps and touches in Coleman's favor if they have any hope of digging out of being a bottom-10 rushing offense. That's good and bad. It's good in that a team acquiring him via trade wouldn't necessarily be locked to Dobbins beyond 2026, unless he were to arrive and hit it out of the park. Now, it's helpful that nearly half of the 2026 season is over, so the Broncos have already absorbed a good chunk of his contract, and they've already paid out his $4 million signing bonus. That simplifies things somewhat for an interested suitor that's mostly concerned with running back help this season, and less worried about 2027. J.K. Following the game, he purportedly didn't make himself available to reporters in the locker room, further showing his frustration. Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman Broncos' Most Surprising Trade Candidate Is Hiding in Plain Sight Skip to main content SI.COM J.K. Dobbins doesn't seem happy at the moment. The Denver Broncos' veteran running back received a season-low 14 snaps in Week 7's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals. With rookie Jonah Coleman returning from injured reserve, Dobbins took a back seat in the desert, both in snap and touch share. The Broncos' offense looked different with Coleman on the field , and his versatility as a receiver and as a pass protector gives Sean Payton so much more to work with. When Coleman is on the field, opponents can't be sure whether it's a run or a pass coming, while with Dobbins and RJ Harvey, defenses can play the probabilities more accurately. Dobbins doesn't appear to be taking this development well, and if he's unable to get his mind right, the Broncos could suddenly become amenable to trading him away . Several teams have serious running back issues right now — including the New York Giants, who've already orchestrated a big trade (quarterback J.J. McCarthy). home.blurb: Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was a limited participant in practice, taking the field for the first time since tweaking his hamstring in Week 4. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was a limited participant in practice after being designated to return from the Physically Unable to Perform list on Wednesday . He was placed on the list before training camp began after tearing his ACL last season. He has a 21-day practice window before the Chiefs must sign him to the active 53-man roster. Denver defensive backs Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga, both nursing ankle injuries, have a chance to return. Hufanga is projected to be out two to three weeks, and this is the third week of that timeline. Surtain enters Week 4 of his rehab, which could be the ideal time to return. After all, it's Kansas City week. Their returns would be timely. picks.headline: Patriots opponent preview: Are the Dolphins trending up?
picks.blurb: Patriots opponent preview: Are the Dolphins trending up? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers win World Series NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Patriots opponent preview: Are the Dolphins trending up? Bernd Buchmasser Wed, October 28, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off their mini-bye, the New England Patriots return to their division. On Sunday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will visit the Dolphins in Miami. The Dolphins are in the middle of a rebuild. They brought in Jeff Hafley and Malik Willis as the head coach-quarterback combo this offseason to replace the departed Mike McDaniel and Tua Tagovailoa, and have invested heavily in rookie talent: no team made more picks in this year's draft than Miami's 13. The organization is building for the future, even though there are some current growing pains. At 1-5 and ranked 30th in scoring differential thus far, the Dolphins have been one of the worst teams in the NFL this season up to that point. That said, they might be trending up. Let's meet them. Dolphins key stats The Dolphins' problems are reflected by their statistics. They are ranked near the bottom of the league in most major categories on both offense and defense. 1-5 (4th AFCE) 4-3 (2nd AFCE) Scoring diff. Points allowed/game Off. yards/game Off. EPA/play -0.122 (29th) Off. EPA/dropback -0.116 (28th) -0.130 (20th) -0.200 (26th) Def. yards/game Def. EPA/play Def. EPA/dropback -0.115 (13th) -0.081 (22nd) Turnover diff. Offensively, the Dolphins have struggled moving the ball both through the air and on the ground. There have been flashes, but the consistency is lacking even though the team has been able to keep turnovers in a comparatively reasonable range (especially when looking to New England's much more talented offense). On defense, a lack of takeaway has plagued the unit, as has an uneven pass rush and an inability to get off the field on third down (52.1%; 31st). The run defense has been a relative bright spot, but considering that opponents are throwing all over the Dolphins — fourth-most attempts (175), highest net yards per attempt (7.5), highest scoring percentage (49.1%) — there simply is no need to run into a veteran D-line on a regular basis. Dolphins 2026 season The Dolphins started their season with five straight losses, including the first three by multiple scores. Since then, however, they have shown some improvement. Their scoring margin of -7 over the last three games is a distinct improvement, as is being able to finally earn a victory last Sunday against the lackluster Jets. Week 1: 27-13 loss at Las Vegas Raiders (0-1) Week 2: 35-13 loss at San Francisco 49ers (0-2) Week 3: 24-10 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs (0-3) Week 4: 15-10 loss at Minnesota Vikings (0-4) Week 5: 31-24 loss vs. Cincinnati Bengals (0-5) Week 6: Bye Week 7: 28-25 win at New York Jets (1-5) What stands out about Miami's schedule is that it featured the last three unbeaten teams in the league — the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings — and the toughest strength of schedule among all 32 teams (.667). Granted, the Dolphins being fairly bad played into that, but they have played, and lost to, some very good teams and beaten the worst one they have faced so far. Dolphins active roster Roster up-to-date as of Oct. 28, 5 a.m. ET | *denotes nominal starter Quarterback (2): Malik Willis* (2), Kyle McCord (14) Running back (3): Ollie Gordon II* (0), Jaylen Wright (5 | KR), Kaytron Allen (30) Fullback (1): D.J. Herman (34) Wide receiver (6): Malik Washington* (6 | PR), Chris Bell* (18), Caleb Douglas* (7), Kevin Coleman Jr. (21), Jared Wayne (86), Jalen Tolbert (1) Tight end (4): Greg Dulcich* (85), Will Kacmarek (89), Seydou Traore (83), Justin Joly (80) Offensive tackle (4): Patrick Paul* (52 | LT), Austin Jackson* (73 | RT), Caedan Wallace (77), Chukwuebuka Godrick (79) Interior offensive line (6): Kadyn Proctor* (74 | LG), Aaron Brewer* (55 | C), Jonah Savaiinaea* (71 | RG), Jarrett Kingston (62), Andrew Meyer (60), D.J. Campbell (63) Interior defensive line (4): Zach Sieler* (92), Jordan Phillips* (94), Kenneth Grant (78), Zeek Biggers (93) Defensive edge (5): Joshua Uche* (9), Chop Robinson* (44), Malik Herring (90), Rob Beal Jr. (51), Rodney McGraw (59) Linebacker (5): Jacob Rodriguez* (10), Jordyn Brooks* (20), Willie Gay Jr. (40), Jackson Woodard (42), Shaka Heyward (45) Cornerback (6): Chris Johnson* (3), Jason Marshall Jr.* (4), JuJu Brents* (8), Jaylin Simpson (32), Reese Taylor (35), Marcellas Dial Jr. (24) Safety (5): Michael Taaffe* (16), Dante Trader Jr.* (11), Zayne Anderson (23), Julius Wood (25), Kyle Louis (19) Specialists (2): Bradley Pinion (48 | P/H), LS Tucker Addington (46 | LS) The first thing that stands out about the Dolphins is their commitment to rebuilding from the ground up. As part of that process, they have six rookie starters in their lineup: wide receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas and left guard Kadyn Proctor on offense, plus linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, cornerback Chris Johnson and safety Michael Taaffe on defense. Furthermore, several of their key reserves are first-year players as well, including fullback D.J. Herman, WR4 Kevin Coleman Jr, and their entire three-man backup tight end group. How soon the Dolphins will add a quarterback to the mix will be seen. For now, however, they are riding with free agency signing Malik Willis. Willis has started all six of the team's games since signing a three-year, $67.5 million contract to move from Green Bay to Miami alongside his head coach. In those games, he has completed 87 o f 151 pass attempts (57.6%) for 1,057 yards with four touchdowns and interceptions each. He also has been sacked 16 times and scored three rushing touchdowns. Willis is a hit-or-miss thrower with big-play potential, but overall has been uneven as evidenced by his 31st ranking among quarterbacks in EPA per play (-0.115). Part of the reason might be his supporting cast, which is missing its best player — running back De'Von Achane — and relying on a whole lot of young talent. That said, Willis' top two receivers this year are both veterans: wide receiver Malik Washington (26/289/0) and tight end Greg Dulcich (18/213/0). At running back, meanwhile, Ollie Gordon has stepped up since Achane's season-ending knee injury. He has carried the. ball 72 times for 339 yards and a 4.7-yard average per carry; Gordon also has scored a team-leading four times. Miami's offensive line, meanwhile, is a collection of highly-drafted players. The only non-first- or second-round pick is center Aaron Brewer, a former undrafted free agent who started his career with Mike Vrabel's Titans in 2020. On the other side of the ball, Miami is led by a veteran defensive line. The top players among the group are Zach Sieler and Chop Robinson, who are tied for the team lead with two sacks each. Robinson, meanwhile, has posted a team-high 20 quarterback pressures. Also high on both lists is ex-Patriot and started edge Joshua Uche, who has one quarterback takedown among his 13 pressures. The second level of the defense is led by the aforementioned Jacob Rodriguez, who has impressed since arriving in the second round of this year's draft. His running mate off the ball is first-team All-Pro Jordyn Brooks, who signed a three-year, $48.1 million extension through 2029 this offseason. The Dolphins are banking on Rodriguez and Brooks leading their defense for years to come, and for good reason: both are very good players. The secondary doesn't have the same consistent talent, even though it has received some solid contributions from its youngsters and veterans alike. Safety Michael Taaffe, for example, is leading the team with two interceptions and tied for the team lead with a forced fumble. Overall, however, as illustrated by the EPA per dropback ranking, the Dolphins' pass defense has some ground to make up — and an inconsistent secondary is a big reason for that. Interestingly enough, the Dolphins don't have a kicker on their active roster. Riley Patterson was released after missing three kicks over the first five games, with the team relying on practice squad member Zane Gonzalez since. In his lone game, Gonzalez has not attempted any field goals but gone a perfect 4-for-4 on extra points. Dolphins reserves Practice squad (16): QB Brady Cook (15), RB Carlos Washington Jr. (26), WR A.J. Henning (82), WR Jalen Reagor (88), WR Will Sheppard (81), TE Tre Watson (87), OT Gottlieb Ayedze (72), OL James Easter (65), DT Jordan Jefferson (91), ED Amari Gainer (53), ED Max Llewellyn (57), ED Eric Watts (95), LB Liam Anderson (50), CB Ethan Bonner (27), S Major Burns (43), K Zane Gonzalez (31) IR (6): RB De'Von Achane (28), TE Cole Turner (87), DT Rene Konga (95), LB Ronnie Harrison (56), LB Trey Moore (17) PUP (1): CB Darrell Baker Jr. (22) The most prominent name on the Dolphins' reserve lists is without a doubt De'Von Achane, who will miss the remainder of the season with a torn ACL suffered in Week 3. Coming off a season in which he had 1,838 scrimmage yards and 12 touchdowns, a healthy Achane would be Miami's lead running back and most dangerous offensive player. Dolphins coaching staff Head coach: Jeff Hafley Coordinators: Bobby Slowik (OC), Sean Duggan (DC), Chris Tabor (ST) The Dolphin overhauled their coaching staff this offseason, firing Mike McDaniel and brining in Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley. Patriots might know Hafley from another role, though: he was Boston College's head coach between 2020 and 2023. Hafley brought coordinator Sean Duggan and a significant portion of the defensive staff with him, and also hired Chris Tabor to lead the special teams unit. On offense, there is a bit more continuity: coordinator Bobby Slowik already was with the Dolphins under McDaniel, previously serving as a senior passing game coordinator.

I think this is the first game since the first week [it’s] going to be all of us out there. The most notable name still with an injury designation is Miami native cornerback Carlton Davis III , who has been dealing with a neck injury that he suffered in Week 1. “Yeah, I mean it’s everything,” said Gonzalez. away.headline: Patriots week 8 injury report: Great news across the board
away.blurb: As the result of extended time from last Thursday's loss to Chicago, positive light has been shined on an injury riddled Patriots team — which is RotoWire's eighth-highest ranked team when it comes to injury impacts. On the first injury report of Week 8, the Patriots have their least amount of limited or non-participants since Week 1's opening practice. Three immediate pieces that standout on the injury report is the return of cornerbacks Carlton Davis, Channing Canada, and Karon Prunty. The three have each missed four games this season, leaving the cornerback room to rely on star Christian Gonzalez — who's also faced injury troubles this season — Marcus Jones, and Charles Woods. "I'm happy to be back out here and be a full go," said Davis ahead of Wednesday's practice. The Patriots offensive line drills had Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse starting. The fifth and sixth options at guard made their debuts in the starting five last Thursday against the Bears. With Alijah Vera-Tucker on injured reserve and Ben Brown listed as questionable, at the moment, it seems the two will keep their position as the starting inside offensive linemen. On the outside, Morgan Moses is listed as limited with a foot injury for the second week in a row. After sustaining the injury against the Jets, Moses activation against Chicago came as somewhat of a surprise, as the 35-year-old was able to play the entire game. Still listed as limited six days later, his status will be one to watch in the coming days. Another thing to note is Marcus Bryant's full participation on Wednesday. He's been out since the start of the season and is still on the injured reserve, though his IR activiation period is coming to a close soon — meaning the Patriots will have to decide whether they use one of their five remaining injured reserve activations for the season on Bryant. Brown is listed with an ankle injury and was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. His ankle injury is the same one he suffered in Week 1 against Seattle that landed him on injured reserve. In the seven practice appearances since Brown's return to play, he's only been a full participant once (the Wednesday before the Bears' game where the Patriots held a walk-through). While the Pats have been mindful of Brown's ankle, there could be more explanation to his limited status. Not only does it leave uncertainty for Miami's defense which is preparing for a dwindled receiver room that is likely to rely on Brown, but a lighter Wednesday practice leaves room for Brown to participate in most drills in a limited capacity. The New England Patriots returned to practice on Wednesday after a day off to continue game preparation for Week 8's match against the Miami Dolphins (1-5). home.headline: Breaking Down a New Willis Issue and the Two Concussions on the Dolphins' Lengthy Injury Report
home.blurb: Only two players on the active roster missed the first practice ahead of the team's Week 8 game against the New England Patriots, but both rookie guard Kadyn Proctor and cornerback JuJu Brents were out because they're in the concussion protocol. The injury report, though, featured eight players listed as limited participants. The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee). Only Trader had an injury reported in the press box Sunday, so it's possible than any of the other four were injured in practice. The most prominent players among those who were limited were wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) and starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot). How the Dolphins' Injury Status Shapes Up Coming Out of the Bye If the Miami Dolphins are going to make it two in a row after getting their first victory of the season, they might have to overcome some injury issues. Because of the fickle nature of concussions, it's impossible to predict whether either or both will be able to play against the Patriots, and Brents was spotted on the outside practice fields at the Baptist Health Training Complex doing conditioning work, which clearly is a good sign. The first injury report of the week for the Dolphins was a long one with 13 names on it, and a new issue for quarterback Malik Willis. After earlier this season being listed with a toe issue and then with a thumb injury, this time Willis is dealing with a groin injury, although he was a full participant in practice Wednesday. Another full participant was edge defender Rob Beal Jr., who has missed the past four games because of a hamstring injury. On the list was cornerback Reese Taylor, who missed the past three games with a quad injury, and long-snapper Tucker Addington and tight end Will Kacmarek both were on the injury report last week before playing in the 28-25 victory against the New York Jets. Head coach Jeff Hafley revealed the concussions before practice before taking questions from the assembled media. Hafley also indicated that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium. Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53. If Brents can't play against New England, then Jason Marshall Jr. would take his place in a normal (four-DB) defensive alignment and Jaylin Simpson likely would be the choice to line up outside with Marshall if/when the Dolphins want to slide rookie Chris Johnson in the slot in the nickel. home.headline: Patriots’ Carlton Davis III Shares Encouraging Injury Update Before Dolphins Game
home.blurb: “I'm happy to be back out here and be a full go,” Davis said, as quoted by the Boston Herald ‘s Doug Kyed . Davis spoke Wednesday as the Patriots prepared for their trip to Miami. Davis also said he came back too soon from the neck injury and made it worse, according to MassLive ‘s Mark Daniels . The setback kept him out of the Patriots' last three games. The neck problem surfaced in Week 1, when Davis left briefly against the Seattle Seahawks after a tackle. He missed Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers after the Patriots downgraded him from questionable to out . Davis missed Week 5 against the Las Vegas Raiders and Week 6 against the New York Jets . He practiced on a limited basis before Week 7 against the Chicago Bears, but the Patriots ruled him out of the 30-24 Thursday night loss, according to Patriots.com reporter Evan Lazar . The Patriots' available corners against Chicago were Jones, Woods, Kindle Vildor and Gonzalez, with rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada sidelined by hamstring injuries. That losing skid is a record during the Nick Sirianni era and longest since 2016, when Carson Wentz was a QB prodigy in his rookie season. That was also the season Lane Johnson missed 10 games because of a PED suspension. The Eagles went 2-8 without him. This season, Johnson retired. So far, the Eagles are 0-4 without him. Johnson isn't coming back. Neither is quarterback Jalen Hurts, who's presumably out for the season to treat blood clots that have traveled to both of his lungs. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets The Cowboys exposed all of that, including an AWOL defense that couldn't stop the run as the Cowboys rushed for 204 yards, or pass as Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns. But there were positives that the Eagles can build on heading into their Nov. 1 matchup against the Commanders . The game between the 2-5 Eagles and the 1-4-1 Commanders is the Sunday Night Football game. This probably won't be a ratings bonanza. Unless, of course, viewers like watching two teams battle it out for the opposite of NFC East supremacy. The Eagles won the first game 24-22 in the season opener on Sept. 13. Still, the Eagles' offense had perhaps its best game, or at least its best 2½ quarters, of the season. The Eagles scored touchdowns on their first two possessions, something they haven't done all season. They also scored a touchdown on their opening drive of the third quarter, again a first for the season. picks.blurb: 1. Philadelphia needs a reset: The Eagles have dropped five straight after a 2-0 start, with Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys moving them to 2-5. Another division loss would make an already difficult climb even steeper for a team that's more realistically already on to 2027 due to so many key injuries. 2. Keep an eye on Saquon: Speaking of injuries, Saquon Barkley played only nine snaps Monday while dealing with hamstring and back issues. He offered an encouraging assessment of his hamstring and said he doesn't expect the back problem to keep him out. His practice workload still warrants watching. 3. The preparation advantage favors Washington: The Commanders come off their bye, while the Eagles turn around from Monday night for a Sunday road game. That's valuable extra time to prepare for Tanner McKee and the Eagles' reshuffled offense. 4. McKee needs help from his defense: Philadelphia's quarterback threw for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. The Eagles produced three touchdown drives, but their defense couldn't slow the Cowboys. Sustaining drives only helps so much if the other team keeps answering. 5. We should expect points: With a game total around 40.5, we're not asking for much to hit 41 points, even from these two offenses. The trends are on our side. Commanders coach Dan Quinn is 8-1 to the over in division games since the start of last season, while the Eagles are 7-1 to the over against the Commanders under coach Nick Sirianni. Saquon Barkley aggravated his hamstring and played only nine snaps, leaving another major question around an offense already operating without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee can keep things functional when the Eagles protect him and stay balanced. That becomes much harder if the Commanders take away the run and force longer passing situations. Washington also has the benefit of a bye and lots of extra rest, while Philadelphia turns around from Monday night. It's so disappointing this is a primetime game. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Eagles 19, Commanders 14 Seldom has prime time featured two teams facing such desperation around midseason. The severely shorthanded Eagles offense finally showed signs of life against the Cowboys, though the once-reliable defense suffered perhaps its worst performance of the Vic Fangio era. Expect a bounce-back outing against a Washington team short on weapons. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Commanders 23, Eagles 13 The Commanders haven't won a game that Jayden Daniels started in since Oct. 5, 2025. Washington is 0-7-1 in the eight starts after that victory, but the time has come as the team comes out of the bye. They have run out of alarms to describe the fire on Dan Quinn's seat, making this contest a must-win for the Commanders to have any chance of making the playoffs in a weak NFC East. Against a battered and bruised Eagles squad that is running out of players, there is no better time for Washington to get back in the win column. away.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley Weighs In On Potential 18-Game NFL Season Amid Injury Concerns
away.blurb: In March, ESPN's Stephen Holder reported the NFLPA took a public stance against expanding the schedule to 18 games. However, Holder pointed out it did so before the schedule expanded to 17 games as well before eventually agreeing to a new collective bargaining agreement. Count Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley among those who are against the NFL expanding to 18 regular-season games. "I can't speak on how players feel," Barkley told Dan Roberts of Front Office Sports (9:55 mark). "How do I feel about it? I'm not a fan of it. I actually don't agree with it, to be completely honest. "Yeah, and so if it's up to me and up to my vote on that particular thing that they want to change, I don't think so. … I'm all about players' health. And I don't see how any way adding another game is advantageous to our health for the now and for the future." Eagles' Top Trade Assets 🏷️ He highlighted the physical wear and tear of the sport, including at his running back position. "But me personally, if you talk about the best way I can answer it for player safety, I don't see how adding another game is good for player safety," Barkley continued. "And that's just kind of my stance on it. But I know some people agree and a lot of people disagree with it." The comments were particularly notable coming from Barkley, who has dealt with a hamstring injury this season. Mark Maske of Front Office Sports noted the league and team owners are eventually expected to propose expanding the regular-season schedule to 18 games, although any official discussions are on hold while JC Tretter, who is the union's executive director, talks to players on team visits. The NFL expanded to 17 games starting with the 2021 season. If the league wanted to expand the schedule again before the current CBA expires after the 2030 season, it would have to negotiate with the union and surely offer other concessions. home.headline: Eagles Week 8 injury report: 6 players listed as DNP ahead of Commanders game
home.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles opened their Week 8 preparations Wednesday with an extensive injury report, listing six players as nonparticipants and another six as limited participants ahead of Sunday's NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders . Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. Philadelphia held a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice, so Wednesday's injury report estimated how players would have participated in a full session. The report included 19 players, with running back Saquon Barkley, wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, linebacker Jihaad Campbell, wide receiver Britain Covey, and cornerback Jonathan Jones all listed as nonparticipants. The injury comes at a difficult time for Philadelphia, which has lost five straight games and struggled to produce consistently on offense. Barkley's availability will be particularly important against Washington as the Eagles attempt to establish a balanced offense with Tanner McKee under center. Philadelphia's receiving corps also remains a concern. Smith was listed as a nonparticipant because of a hamstring injury, while Wicks continues to deal with an ankle injury. Both receivers missed Monday night's loss to Dallas, leaving rookie Makai Lemon and the team's remaining pass catchers to handle expanded responsibilities. Greenard continues to deal with an ankle injury, while Hunt was listed with knee and ankle injuries. home.blurb: Three Injured Washington Commanders Return to Practice CommandersRoundtable 141 Members • 1,206 Posts CommandersRoundtable CommandersRoundtable Related stories Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Three Injured Washington Commanders Return to Practice Ahmed Ghafir Partner Oct 26, 2026 6:22 PM Published Oct 26, 2026 6:22 PM Updated Oct 26, 2026 6:43 PM Defensive end Charles Omenihu is one of three players the Washington Commanders saw return to practice on Monday ahead of the week eight primetime meeting against the Philadelphia Eagles Head coach Dan Quinn noted that quarterback Marcus Mariota and defensive end Charles Omenihu will return to practice on Monday. The veteran quarterback went down in the week four loss against the Indianapolis Colts in London with what the team described as a knee injury, allowing rookie Athan Kaliakmanis to make his NFL debut after replacing him before Mariota avoided injury reserve. Omenihu has missed the last two games with a groin/ankle injury, marking a welcomed return for the defensive line's depth. Yet there was some bad news after Quinn revealed defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw remains sidelined as head coach Dan Quinn noted his recovery has not materialized as hoped. Kinlaw has battled through injuries in his second season with the franchise despite not missing any games yet, though whether he will ultimately be available in week eight remains to be seen. On the flip side, how healthy the Eagles are in week eight remains to be seen with defensive back Michael Carter, wide receiver DeVonta Smith, outside linebacker Nolan Smith and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks all ruled out for the Monday night matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in week seven. That doesn't include running back Saquon Barkley among the over dozen of Eagles who drew the questionable tag in the latest injury report, while head coach Nick Sirianni is still battling through the sudden retirement of All-Pro offensive tackle Lane Johnson. Quarterback Tanner McKee is also set to start in week seven with Jalen Hurts sidelined for the remainder of the season. More Videos The Washington Commanders are fresh off the bye week and will shift their attention toward the second consecutive primetime game with a home game against the Philadelphia Eagles set for week eight. The Commanders will also enter the divisional game a bit more healthy, too. Quinn also noted that wide receiver Treylon Burks, who left the week six loss in the closing minutes due to injury, will also work his way back into practice with a chance to elevate the unit's depth. Burks will loom large as head coach Dan Quinn noted that it will be the rest of the Commanders' wide receivers who will be asked to step up to mitigate the season-ending loss of veteran Terry McLaurin . With the target share not expected to change for Stefon Diggs, Quinn also pointed to rookie Antonio Williams as one who can elevate his role in the offense after flashing through his first six games.
